dinkum-3.meaning: All points kept: the remarkable group, the unprecedented opportunity, talented colleagues, the culture, partnering across government, strategic and practical, open iterative delivery, feedback, thanks. "If we can't work with colleagues across government, we can't make a difference, simple as that." restates "crucial" a little more absolutely.
dinkum-3.sense: Fits well ("a cracking bunch of people", "We're having a red-hot go at leading the way", "give us a yell", "We’re stoked to have you"); "being a good mate to our colleagues" is slightly informal for "partner" but fits.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural Australian workplace voice: "keeping our feet on the ground with the nitty gritty", "we're dead set on working in an open, iterative and user-centred way".
dinkum-3.register: Level 3, with one mild swear ("bloody talented") within vulgarity 1.
dinkum-3.tone: Warm and welcoming throughout, as the original.
dinkum-3.flow: Reads easily: "That chance is what brings us all together, and it's what keeps us fired up about the job."
dinkum-3.variety: Varied: "cracking bunch", "fired up", "care heaps", "red-hot go", "dead set", "give us a yell", "stoked".

unharnessed.meaning: Points kept, but "We've got a once-in-a-lifetime chance to drag our government into the digital" shifts "unprecedented" to a one-off; "inclusive, open, respectful and upbeat" folds "transparent" into "open" fairly.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly fits ("a ripper bunch of people", "give us a yell"), but "we try to show" off the culture turns "exemplify" into showing off, the wrong sense; "top-notch partner" fits.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural, though some stretches stay corporate ("Being able to work well with colleagues across government is crucial to us making a").
unharnessed.register: Close to level 3 but lighter in the middle paragraphs; mild swear "bloody talented" within vulgarity 1.
unharnessed.flow: Smooth, though "is crucial to us making a" difference is stiff.

yarn-troppo.meaning: Gist kept, but additions change claims: "doing the sort of work you'll be telling your grandkids about", "Can't do it on our own.", "yours included"; "nothing's hidden" and "we keep our chins up" reinterpret "transparent" and "upbeat".
yarn-troppo.sense: "we keep our chins up" implies cheerfulness in the face of hardship, not a generally upbeat culture; "keeping our boots on the" ground is a military idiom; "they really give a stuff about making a difference" fits.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Much is natural ("getting particular projects over the line", "don't sit on it: sing out"), but "Well, g'day and welcome." and "talented as" lean stagey.
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 3, nearer 4: "Here's the thing:", "good and proper", "the whole show", "mind;". "give a stuff" is within vulgarity 1.
yarn-troppo.tone: Warm, but the jokey hype ("telling your grandkids about") tips the sincere welcome into salesy banter.
yarn-troppo.flow: Some pile-ups: "bringing our government into the digital age, good and proper, and changing the way the whole show works".
yarn-troppo.variety: Very varied: "cracking bunch", "hard yards", "give a stuff", "walk the walk", "over the line", "delivering the goods", "sing out".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the letter, though overlaid with added patter.

engine.meaning: Every point survives, because the text is the original almost verbatim ("We have an unprecedented opportunity to bring our government into the digital").
engine.sense: "being a bloody great partner" works as an intensifier, but "We aim to make our bloody organisation as agile" reads as exasperation with the organisation, the wrong sense.
engine.authenticity: Mechanical: two swears dropped into untouched US corporate prose ("user-centered" kept).
engine.register: Barely translated, apart from the swears and "organisation". Swears stay within vulgarity 1.
engine.tone: The warm tone survives, but "our bloody organisation" sounds fed-up, undercutting a welcome letter.
engine.flow: Readable, as the original; the inserted "bloody"s jar.
engine.essence: The original letter with two insertions.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Points kept; "Welcome aboard." is a natural opener, but "doing work that'd" make anyone proud shifts "inspiring" to "proud", and "We reckon our organisation should be" softens "We aim" slightly.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Fits well ("a top bunch of people", "a seriously talented, hard-working lot", "just sing out"); "being a ripper partner to our colleagues right across" government is an odd collocation.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural Australian office voice: "keeping our feet on the" ground, "We're stoked to" have you.
yarn-dinkum.register: Level 3 as asked; no swearing (allowed up to 1).
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth: "That chance is what brings us together, and" it keeps us fired up.
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "top bunch", "fired up", "hard-working lot", "ripper", "hand in hand", "sing out", "stoked".
